newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo banks say cenbank measure to raise insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo banks say cenbank measure to raise insolvency.

text.p: Yugoslav banks called on the central bank to reconsider its decision to impose a 10 percent reserve requirement on all commercial bank deposits, warning it would push many of them into the red.

"It is a big blow to banks' liquidity. It will halt all credit activity and push interest rates up," Beogradska Banka General Manager Ljubisa Igic told a meeting of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Executive Board on Friday.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) introduced the reserve requirement, which took effect on September 11, to reduce and control money supply that it said had grown too much over the past two months.
Cash-strapped commercial banks criticised the stringent requirement for not differentiating between various types of deposits.
Bankers also said the move would raise the price of capital, steering it away from legal channels "to the black zone."

"These acrobatics in the monetary sphere could have serious repercussions on economic stability," Igic said. "They may yield short-term results, but in the long run they lead to an inflationary explosion."
The Association of Yugoslav Banks on Thursday said the NBY's decision would rock the banks' already shaky liquidity and should be implemented selectively and gradually.
Just one day after it was introduced, banks paid some 200 million dinars into the central bank's coffers, cutting their positive balance to around 134 million, the association said.
But NBY vice-governor Ratko Banovic insisted the measure would remain in place.

"The NBY's task is to control money supply. This is part of a package of measures and we will observe their overall effect. If necessary we will make corrections along the way," Banovic said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
